parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs output, manual argv parsing, exact stdout/stderr/exit-code parity, bencode encode/decode behavior, BigInt integer handling, and no external dependencies. The workflow brief also added an internal no-Buffer constraint.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent first probed and wrote SPEC.md, then launched one workflow. The workflow assigned four spec-only children and one later implementation child; downstream differential, repair, and audit phases were owned by the workflow script.
parallel.implementation: The implementation child wrote /output/test12.mjs and eight library modules, ran sample, CLI, unicode, byte, Nd digit, and fuzz tests, while the parent independently tested the generated files and found a traceback source-line defect.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The implementation child wrote directly to shared /output. Artifacts were copied successfully, but the workflow never returned buildReport and final.txt is empty because the parent process timed out.
parallel.verification: Parallel evidence includes the four documented sample cases passing, 40 and 32 case parent batches passing, then 17 unicode/length mismatches found by the parent, plus child-reported larger passing batches before interruption.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with the implementer still in progress. Planned workflow differential and audit phases did not complete, and the current official evaluator reports solution_passed false at 142/172.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual CLI, bencode, repr, BigInt, no external dependency, and executable-reference requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor performed environment checks, black-box probes, module writing, repairs, and test harness work without delegation or child result joins.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote a hierarchical tree under /output, including bencode encoder/decoder, Python-like int/repr/bytes/errors/linecache helpers, argparse, and test12.mjs, then rewrote argparse after differential failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All writes occurred sequentially in the same actor; artifacts were copied successfully and included test12.mjs plus library modules. final.txt is empty because the process timed out.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran sample and edge probes, built a differential harness, saw 17 failures, repaired traceback behavior, saw 11 remaining failures, added classifier cases, saw program-name diffs, and normalized the harness rather than completing a clean final acceptance.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process also timed out. The current official evaluator reports solution_passed false at 142/172, so its local repair loop did not produce a fully accepted solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized exact Python behavior, ESM .mjs files, local imports, manual argv parsing, BigInt, and black-box executable probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same shared prompt requirements and probed representative happy path, error, repr, unicode, and argparse cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material official requirement-recognition gap is visible; the parallel workflow additionally imposed a no-Buffer internal rule that was stricter than the prompt text.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into four spec lenses followed by a single implementation child, with later differential, repair, and audit phases scripted after the build result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, repair, and verification in one actor and moved from probes to direct file writes without delegated ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-owned critical implementation path and child-result dependency; serial had direct single-owner continuity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel transferred a large SPEC_DIGEST into the implementation child and specified output file layout, imports, CLI, bencode, repr, and audit expectations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained probe findings inside the same actor and used them directly while writing and editing the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing child brief or missing interface contract is proven; the meaningful contrast is that parallel placed the build behind a large child handoff while serial kept context local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child generated test12.mjs and flat lib modules, then continued self-verifying and fuzzing; the parent later identified a traceback-source-line defect in errors.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial generated a deeper lib hierarchy, added linecache support, rewrote argparse parsing, and reached a state where its harness showed remaining diffs as program-name text.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced artifacts and both left hidden evaluator failures; serial visibly completed more local repair steps, while parallel implementation remained an unreturned child task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The four spec child results reached the workflow, but the implementation child had only a start record and was still in progress when the workflow was killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; intermediate results were local files and command outputs immediately visible to the same actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure depended on a child result that never returned; serial closure depended only on local continuation and still timed out.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child wrote directly to /output while the parent read and tested those shared files; no concrete overwrite or collision between live agents is proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote /output sequentially from one actor, with no concurrent child writers or cross-agent file ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared workspace across parent and child for inspection, but the adverse issue was unfinished child ownership rather than a write collision or contamination.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent saw sample and broad batches pass, then found 17 unicode/length mismatches; the workflow planned additional differential and audit phases but never reached them.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a differential suite, repaired issues, reran it, added more classifier cases, and then normalized remaining program-name diffs rather than producing a final clean acceptance record.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had delegated but incomplete verification governance; serial had local verification progress but also no accepted final state. Both official evaluations failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used five subagents and 283716 workflow-child tokens; the process returned 143 after the 2399-second timeout with workflow status killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, had workflows disabled, and also returned 143 after the 2399-second timeout with the same official score.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget, but parallel spent that budget through a workflow whose implementation child never returned, while serial spent it in one local repair loop.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial scored 142/172 and solution_passed false. The main concrete difference is process shape. Parallel delegated spec discovery to four children and placed the full implementation plus heavy verification into one later child that never returned before the workflow was killed. Serial did comparable work locally and reached direct repairs and harness normalization, but still timed out and failed officially. The retained pattern is therefore adverse parallel coordination, not an explanation for a pass/fail split.
parallel_contributors: The implementation child held indispensable build and verification work and was still in progress when the workflow was killed.
The workflow never reached its scripted differential, repair, and audit phases after the build child.
serial_contributors: The serial actor kept implementation and repair local and rewrote argparse after observed mismatches.
The serial actor also timed out without a final clean acceptance despite reaching program-name normalization in its harness.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial artifact used a deeper module hierarchy and visible linecache repair; the parallel artifact used a flatter module layout and the parent observed a Unicode traceback source-line defect.
Both attempts left enough behavioral mismatch for the official evaluator to mark solution_passed false.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both-fail process contrast; no official outcome differential

candidates.reason: Parallel explicitly assigned implementation to the build child, so implementation was owned even though that owner did not finish.

The workflow script owned the end-to-end sequence from spec through build, differential testing, repair, and audit; it failed by timeout, not absent ownership.
There was no single mandatory preflight gate; the workflow used four parallel spec investigations before build, making Serial Investigation the nearer rejected pseudo-concurrency shape.

The spec-first phase is visible, but the independently retained boundary is the later single overbroad implementation child that could not complete; serial also performed local probing before building, so the investigation gate is not retained as a separate episode.
The critical path was not merely underallocated while auxiliary work consumed capacity; the more specific observed boundary was one overbroad implementation child assignment.

Although five children existed, the evidence does not show collective breadth or retries exhausting budget as the direct event; the four spec children returned and one build child remained unfinished.

The workflow assigned one child the full port plus extensive sample, edge, unicode, bigint, static, and differential self-verification. That child wrote artifacts but was still in progress when the workflow was killed, leaving no returned build report and no completed workflow differential/audit.

candidates.near_match_reason: The kill/interrupt is real but downstream of the same oversized-child episode; choosing Early Child Termination would label the terminal symptom rather than the corrective allocation boundary.
